chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Hadeed and Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from one of his companions, he raised it to Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him).

Regarding a man who was killed and had two guardians, so one of them forgave and the other refused to forgive. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If the one who did not forgive wants to kill, he kills, and returns half the blood-money to the guardians of the killed one for the retaliation from it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling when one heir forgives a murder and the other demands execution?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the principle of individual agency in qisas, establishing that each heir holds an independent right to choose between execution and compensation. It highlights the Shia juristic view that forgiveness by one heir does not bind the others, ensuring that the right to retaliate is preserved for those who desire it, while the financial burden of the forgiving party's share is deducted from the estate. This ruling underscores the balance between retributive justice and the economic reality of blood-money distribution among multiple heirs.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Hadeed and Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Jameel Bin Darraj, from one of his companions,

(It has been narrated) that it was asked from Amir Al Momineen<sup>asws</sup> regarding a man who was killed and for him were two guardians. So one of them forgave and the other one refused to forgive. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If the one who did not forgive want him to be killed, he kills and returns half the wergild to the guardians of the killed one for the retaliation from it’.
